title: Lord! Thou Didst Arise and Say
description: Lord! Thou Didst Arise and Say in Tonic Solfa to MESSIAH (HERALD), doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Henry Hart Milman wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 186, “He Rebuked the Wind and the Sea”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens Double (7.7.7.7 D) (7.7.7.7.7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MESSIAH (HERALD); any other Sevens Double (7.7.7.7 D) tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord! thou didst a-rise and say To the trou-bled wa-ters, Peace! And the tem-pest died a-way; Down they sank, the foam-ing seas, And a calm and heav-ing sleep Spread o'er all the glas-sy deep; All the a-zure lake se-rene Like an-oth-er heaven was seen.

lines: Lord! thou didst arise and say
Down they sank, the foaming seas,
And a calm and heaving sleep
Spread o'er all the glassy deep;
To the billows of the proud!
Quell the fierce and changing crowd!
Then the earth shall find repose
In the world of darkness here.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Henry Hart Milman died in 1868.
credits: Words by Henry Hart Milman (1791–1868), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to MESSIAH (HERALD) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
